title: Tensor surjectivity detects a negative valuation
statement: Let A be a subring of a field K with fraction field K, let B be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field K and normalized valuation v:K^\times\to\mathbf Z, and assume the canonical map A\otimes B\to K is surjective. Then there exists a nonzero x\in A with v(x)<0.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N5 (varieties-lemma-create-globally-generated), proof, induction base case

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer t of B. By [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-ring-characterization], t^{-1} belongs to K^\times and has v(t^{-1})=-1, so it is not in B. Surjectivity of the canonical map A \otimes B \to K gives a finite tensor expression t^{-1}=\sum_{j=1}^r a_j b_j with a_j\in A and b_j\in B.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N5 (varieties-lemma-create-globally-generated), proof, induction base case

proof.text: Suppose, for contradiction, that every nonzero a\in A has v(a)\ge0. Then each nonzero product a_j b_j lies in B: a_j has nonnegative valuation by the supposition, b_j has nonnegative valuation by [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-ring-characterization], v(a_j b_j)=v(a_j)+v(b_j)\ge0 by [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic], and a nonzero element of K of nonnegative valuation lies in B by [lem-sc-dvr-nonnegative-valuation-in-ring]; zero terms are in B as well. Since B is a ring, the finite sum \sum_j a_j b_j lies in B, contradicting that it equals t^{-1}\notin B.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09N5 (varieties-lemma-create-globally-generated), proof, induction base case

proof.text: Therefore some nonzero x=a_j\in A has v(x)<0, which is the required conclusion.
